claim: A relay host can install an exact bounded installation-key signer set and threshold. The exact relay binary preserves rooms without policy but refuses protected remote membership mutations until it receives a unique, valid, project/room/revision/action-bound approval quorum; product controls publish, collect, and submit those approvals without capability copying.
proved: The host-local typed command persists or removes a sorted 1-16 signer policy under an exact registry revision, restarts the relay lifecycle, and rejects stale, invalid, duplicate, and no-op configurations.
A configured room reports schema v4 with threshold, configuration time, and sorted key IDs only; an unconfigured room retains schema v3 and prior managed-administrator behavior.

The relay accepts only unique configured Ed25519 proofs bound to its current project, room, registry revision, and semantic action hash, with relay-clock expiry/future-skew checks and exact signatures.

The exact Rust binary rejects missing, insufficient, duplicate, foreign, wrong-action, wrong-revision, expired, future-dated, and tampered-signature bundles, accepts a two-of-two bundle once, and rejects its stale replay after revision advancement.

Product controls select healthy registered installations, show the threshold and emergency-host boundary, publish an exact approval on attempted remote mutation, report partial quorum, and automatically attach a complete verified bundle on retry.
Read-only shared-state/MCP inspection remains body-free and explicitly refuses to attest host policy because that state is not stored in the shared project.
notProved: That a configured installation key belongs to an authenticated person or organization or represents legal/organizational consent.
Trusted time, approval withdrawal, availability or completeness against a Yjs writer, or a relay-signed approval receipt.
Recovery after every administrator and the relay-host operator are unavailable.
Public WSS operation, third-party relay enforcement, hostile-frame fuzzing, or packaged physical two-install interaction.
